pending_interview.category: System design (ML/AI-specific) — RAG at scale, eval pipeline design, recommendation systems, agent platforms, feature store design
pending_interview.question: You are designing a feature store — a centralized system that computes, stores, and serves the input signals (called "features") that machine learning models use to make predictions — for a large financial services company. The company runs dozens of ML models across fraud detection, credit scoring, and customer churn prediction. Some models need features in real time at the moment a transaction happens (sub-100ms latency). Others are batch models that retrain nightly and just need features to be accurate and available by a certain time each morning. Walk through your high-level architecture for this feature store. How would you handle the difference between real-time and batch feature serving? How would you ensure that the features a model sees during training are the same ones it sees at inference time (a problem sometimes called "training-serving skew")? And how would you handle a situation where a feature pipeline fails partway through — what does the downstream model see, and how do you protect against that?
